60.insights: Cost is 1.0 and the cap is 4.51. Demand is roughly linear in the local range, with a slope of about −98, and the best price is (intercept/98+1)/2. The intercept tracks the competitor's price, which I can't see. It switches between separate levels: about 203.7–203.97, 206.35, 208.7, 210.2 and 213.85. Demand is deterministic once the level is known. 1.58 at 206.35 gave 51.49 units (rounds 27 and 59). 1.47 gave 59.64 units at 203.7 and 61.96 at 206.35. 1.54 gave 53.05 at 203.97 and 55.47 at 206.39. 1.55 gave 61.93 at 213.8, 56.82 at 208.72 and 52.05 at 203.95. 1.56 gave 53.48 at 206.35, 55.84 at 208.7 and 51.05 at 203.93. History of the levels: about 214 in rounds 23–25, 210 in round 26, 206 in rounds 27–28, 213.8 in round 29, 210.2 in rounds 31–39, 206.35 in rounds 40–41, 213.83 in round 43, 208.7 in rounds 44–46, 206.35 in rounds 47–50, about 203.9 in rounds 51–55, 206.39 in round 56, 208.72 in round 57 and 206.35 in rounds 58–59. The level moves between these values rather than steadily trending. Profit is flat near the best price: missing it by 0.05 costs only about 1. Normal profit is about 28–34 per round. Exactly one round per block of 5 is forced. If none has happened by the 4th round of a block, the 5th is certainly forced. When the competitor is forced, the intercept falls to about 191 and my sales fall 27–55% (rounds 15, 18, 30 and 42). The best price in such a round is about 1.48–1.50. My own price was forced in rounds 22, 35, 38, 48, 53 and 58. In those rounds sales follow the normal fit.
